assumptions: you may legally embed the guideline text you retrieve from
a clinician reviews the escalation thresholds before anyone relies on them
no diagnosis or treatment claim is made in your copy
clone_cost.estimate: 1 week for the check-in core, 3-4 weeks with history, handoff and a real eval
clone_cost.why: FastAPI, SQLite, Pydantic and local retrieval are ordinary parts; the work is the guideline corpus, the rule set and the evaluation cases

hazard_note: Risk assessment on a medical condition. The team disclaims diagnosis, states the benchmarks are not clinical validation, and keeps recommendations conservative; that is better hygiene than most of the corpus, not permission to run it on real patients without oversight.

prior_art.relation: parallel invention at the same event under the same name: baseline-relative monitoring, no rules, no retrieval - keep both, and note this one is specified far more tightly
same containment pattern elsewhere: bounded evidence requests and one human-approved mutation step
same 'cite the rule the verdict came from' discipline applied to a different regulated document type

what_breaks_first: The self-graded benchmark: 100% across a case set nobody outside the team defined or counted measures their agreement with themselves, and the page is honest enough to say it is not clinical validation - so a clone inherits the need for a real evaluation with data and a clinician. Second, multi-day history with no persistence story (secure cross-session storage is still on the roadmap).
what_to_steal: Escalation precedence: compute the red-flag rules first and *suppress* the normal path when they fire, rather than letting a friendly assistant narrate its way past a warning sign. Pair it with schema validation of every structured result before it renders, and hand the professional a summary artifact rather than a chat transcript.
worth_note: The architecture is the contribution: deterministic extraction, rule-based history-aware scoring, retrieval over a guideline corpus, and escalation that pre-empts advice - with the generative model kept out of the decision path. That is the correct shape for software that touches a regulated outcome, and it is rare to see it chosen deliberately at hackathon scale. Held below breakthrough because the pieces are standard practice in clinical decision support.
